question: Who among the following is a Jnanpith Award-winning woman writer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahadevi Verma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahadevi Verma was a distinguished Hindi poet and a major pillar of the Chhayavaad (romanticism) movement in Hindi literature (ज्ञानपीठ पुरस्कार विजेता महिला लेखिका).

• She won the Jnanpith Award in 1982 for her poetry collection 'Yama'.

• She is popularly called the 'Modern Meera' of Hindi literature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour, instituted in 1961 and given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith.

• Mahadevi Verma also received the Padma Bhushan (1956) and Padma Vibhushan (1988).

• Her famous works include Neerja, Deepshikha and Sandhya Geet.

NOTE

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 2): Known as the 'Nightingale of India', a poet and freedom fighter, the first woman Governor of an Indian state (UP); she did not win the Jnanpith Award.

• Kamala Surayya (Option 3): Also known as Kamala Das, a Malayalam and English writer; she was nominated for the Nobel Prize but did not win the Jnanpith Award.

• Subhadra Kumari Chauhan (Option 4): A Hindi poet famous for the patriotic poem 'Jhansi Ki Rani'; she did not win the Jnanpith Award.

question: Who assumed the Chairmanship of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in May 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajay Kumar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Ajay Kumar assumed charge as the Chairman of the UPSC in May 2025 (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग के अध्यक्ष).

• He is a former Defence Secretary of India and belongs to the 1985 batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre.

• The UPSC Chairman is appointed by the President of India under Article 316 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The UPSC was established on 1 October 1926 and is a constitutional body under Articles 315-323.

• UPSC members hold office for 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

• The headquarters of UPSC is at Dholpur House, New Delhi.

NOTE

• Preety Sudan (Option 1): A former Union Health Secretary who served as UPSC Chairperson before Ajay Kumar; she is not the May 2025 appointee.

• Manoj Soni (Option 2): A former UPSC Chairman who resigned in 2024 before completing his term.

• Anuj Kumar Singh (Option 3): Not associated with the Chairmanship of the UPSC in May 2025.

question: Arif Mohammad Khan has been appointed as the Governor of _____ in December 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arif Mohammad Khan was appointed as the Governor of Bihar in December 2024 (बिहार के राज्यपाल).

• He earlier served as the Governor of Kerala.

• A Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The office of the Governor is provided under Articles 153-162 of the Constitution.

• In the same reshuffle, Ajay Kumar Bhalla was made Governor of Manipur.

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state and the nominal executive.

NOTE

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Haribhau Kisanrao Bagade was serving as Governor of Rajasthan, not Arif Mohammad Khan.

• Haryana (Option 2): Bandaru Dattatreya was the Governor of Haryana during this period.

• Assam (Option 4): Lakshman Prasad Acharya held additional charge/served as Governor of Assam, not Arif Mohammad Khan.

question: In March 2025, 'Lakhpati Didi Sammelan' was held in the state of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2025, the 'Lakhpati Didi Sammelan' was held in the state of Gujarat (लखपति दीदी सम्मेलन).

• The Lakhpati Didi Scheme aims to make women of Self Help Groups (SHGs) earn a sustainable annual income of at least Rs. 1 lakh.

• The scheme empowers rural women through skilling and financial support.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Lakhpati Didi Yojana was announced in the Independence Day speech of 2023 and expanded in the Interim Budget 2024.

• The scheme is linked with the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).

• The initial target was 2 crore Lakhpati Didis, later raised to 3 crore.

NOTE

• Maharashtra (Option 1): A major state for SHG activity, but the March 2025 Sammelan was not held here.

• Bihar (Option 2): Known for the JEEViKA SHG programme, but not the venue of this event.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Not the state where the March 2025 Lakhpati Didi Sammelan took place.

question: In January 2025, which of the following is NOT among the six cities where the Supreme Court of India banned manual scavenging?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the Supreme Court of India banned manual scavenging in six major metropolitan cities; Jaipur was NOT among them (मैनुअल स्कैवेंजिंग पर प्रतिबंध).

• The six cities were Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

• The Court directed authorities to file affidavits confirming a complete stop to manual scavenging and hazardous sewer cleaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manual scavenging is prohibited under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013.

• The Supreme Court had earlier, in the Balram Singh v. Union of India (2023) judgment, ordered compensation for sewer deaths.

• The NAMASTE Scheme aims to mechanise sanitation work and eliminate hazardous cleaning.

NOTE

• Delhi (Option 1): One of the six cities covered by the Supreme Court's January 2025 ban.

• Bengaluru (Option 2): One of the six cities covered by the ban.

• Chennai (Option 4): One of the six cities covered by the ban.

question: The "Aatmanirbharta in Pulses" campaign, launched in Union Budget 2025, is a government mission spanning _____ years to achieve self-sufficiency in pulse production.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Aatmanirbharta in Pulses" (Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses) was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 as a 6-year mission (दलहन में आत्मनिर्भरता).

• It aims to achieve self-sufficiency in pulse production, focusing on Tur (Arhar), Urad and Masoor.

• Central agencies NAFED and NCCF will procure these pulses from farmers over the next 4 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2025.

• India is the largest producer and consumer of pulses in the world.

• Other Budget 2025 initiatives include the Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana and the National Mission on High Yielding Seeds.

NOTE

• 3 (Option 1): Not the duration of the Aatmanirbharta in Pulses mission.

• 4 (Option 2): This is the procurement period for central agencies, not the total mission span.

• 5 (Option 3): Not the correct duration of the mission.

question: Financial Inclusion Index 2025 was released by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) is compiled and released annually by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक).

• The index captures the extent of financial inclusion across the country on a scale of 0 to 100.

• It is based on three broad parameters: Access, Usage and Quality.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FI-Index was first published by RBI in August 2021.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.

• The current Governor of the RBI is Sanjay Malhotra (took charge in December 2024).

NOTE

• Institute for Competitiveness (Option 2): A research body that prepares indices like the Social Progress Index, not the Financial Inclusion Index.

• CSIR (Option 3): The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, a scientific research organisation, unrelated to this index.

• World Bank (Option 4): An international financial institution; it publishes the Global Findex, not India's FI-Index.

question: Which of the following institution has released the "EnviStats India 2024: Environment Accounts"?
option_1: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
option_4: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "EnviStats India 2024: Environment Accounts" was released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) (सांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयन मंत्रालय).

• It provides environmental statistics compiled under the System of Environmental Economic Accounting (SEEA) framework.

• EnviStats India is published annually to support environmental policy and monitoring.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• MoSPI also releases the GDP data, Consumer Price Index (CPI) and conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).

• The National Statistical Office (NSO) functions under MoSPI.

• MoSPI is currently a stand-alone ministry headed by a Minister of State (Independent Charge).

NOTE

• Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 2): Handles internal security, police and disaster management, not environment accounts.

• Ministry of Cooperation (Option 3): A ministry formed in 2021 for the cooperative sector; unrelated to EnviStats.

• Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Option 4): The nodal environment ministry, but EnviStats is compiled and released by MoSPI.

question: The "Keibul Lamjao National Park", the only floating national park in the world, is in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, is located in Manipur (मणिपुर).

• It floats over the Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in North-East India.

• The floating vegetation mass is locally called 'Phumdis'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The park is the natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer (Brow-antlered deer / Dancing deer), the state animal of Manipur.

• Loktak Lake is a designated Ramsar Site (wetland of international importance).

• The Sangai is also known as the 'Dancing Deer of Manipur'.

NOTE

• Tripura (Option 1): Home to Clouded Leopard National Park, but not Keibul Lamjao.

• Sikkim (Option 3): Known for Khangchendzonga National Park, a World Heritage Site, not a floating park.

• Odisha (Option 4): Known for Bhitarkanika and Simlipal; Chilika Lake is here, but the floating park is in Manipur.

question: The 'Gurjari' raga is traditionally associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Gurjari' raga is traditionally associated with the state of Gujarat (गुजरात).

• The very name 'Gurjari' is derived from the historical region of Gurjaradesa / Gujarat.

• It is a raga referenced in classical Indian music with regional roots in western India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gujarat is famous for folk dances like Garba and Dandiya Raas.

• The classical dance associated with Gujarat's neighbouring cultural traditions includes influences seen in Kathak.

• Ragas in Indian classical music are melodic frameworks assigned to specific moods and times of the day.

NOTE

• Odisha (Option 2): Associated with the classical dance Odissi and Odissi music, not the Gurjari raga.

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for Sopana Sangeetham and dance forms like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

• Goa (Option 4): Known for Mando and Konkani folk traditions, not the Gurjari raga.

question: Who constructed the city of Tughlaqabad?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The city (fort city) of Tughlaqabad was constructed by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty (गयासुद्दीन तुगलक).

• He built it as the third historical city of Delhi in the early 14th century.

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq ruled from 1320 to 1325 CE.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Tughlaq dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1414 CE.

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's original name was Ghazi Malik.

• The Tughlaqabad Fort is known for its massive stone walls and is located in present-day South Delhi.

NOTE

• Alauddin Khilji (Option 1): Ruler of the Khilji dynasty who built the city of Siri and the Alai Darwaza, not Tughlaqabad.

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq (Option 2): Founded the city of Firozabad (Firoz Shah Kotla), not Tughlaqabad.

• Mohammad Bin Tughlaq (Option 3): Son of Ghiyasuddin; he built Jahanpanah and shifted the capital to Daulatabad, but did not build Tughlaqabad.

question: 'Manjira Nritya' is performed by which of the following community in Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padhaar community.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Manjira Nritya' is a folk dance performed by the Padhaar community of Gujarat (पधार समुदाय).

• The dance is named after the 'Manjira', a percussion instrument (small cymbals) used in it.

• The Padhaars live around the Nal Lake region of Gujarat and their dance reflects rowing movements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gujarat's famous folk dances include Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani and Bhavai.

• The Manjira is also used widely in devotional (bhajan) music across India.

• Folk dances of communities often depict their occupation and daily life.

NOTE

• Mappila community (Option 2): A Muslim community of Kerala associated with Mappila songs (Mappila Paattu), not Gujarat.

• Konyak community (Option 3): A major Naga tribe of Nagaland, known for the Aoleang festival.

• Pangal community (Option 4): The Meitei Muslim community of Manipur, not related to Manjira Nritya.

question: In February 2025, which institute has developed solar dehydration technology to boost farmers' income and reduce post-harvest losses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIT Kanpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2025, IIT Kanpur developed a solar dehydration technology to boost farmers' income and reduce post-harvest losses (सौर निर्जलीकरण तकनीक).

• The technology dries agricultural produce using solar energy, preserving fruits, vegetables and spices.

• It helps farmers add value to their produce and reduce wastage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• IIT Kanpur was established in 1959 and is one of the premier IITs of India.

• Post-harvest losses are a major concern in Indian agriculture, affecting perishable crops significantly.

• Solar drying is an eco-friendly, low-cost method of food preservation.

NOTE

• IIT Madras (Option 2): A leading IIT known for various start-ups and research, but not the developer of this technology.

• IIT Bombay (Option 3): Renowned for engineering and research, not associated with this February 2025 development.

• IIT Delhi (Option 4): A top institute, but the solar dehydration technology was developed by IIT Kanpur.

question: Which Tamil Nadu-based startup has developed India's first reusable hybrid rocket, RHUMI-1?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Space Zone India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Space Zone India, a Tamil Nadu (Chennai)-based startup, developed India's first reusable hybrid rocket, RHUMI-1 (स्पेस ज़ोन इंडिया).

• It was launched in collaboration with the Martin Group in August 2024 from Chennai.

• The mission also carried satellites/cubesats using a mobile launcher.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• RHUMI-1 used a hybrid motor and an eco-friendly fuel system, making it cost-effective and reusable.

• The rocket was launched to study atmospheric and environmental conditions.

• It was designed with a generic-fuel-based hybrid propulsion system.

NOTE

• Astra Space (Option 1): Not the developer of RHUMI-1.

• Skyroot Aerospace (Option 3): A Hyderabad-based startup that launched India's first private rocket Vikram-S, not RHUMI-1.

• Agni Aerospace (Option 4): Not associated with the development of RHUMI-1.

question: The Expert Group under the Chairmanship of Dr. C. Rangarajan to Review the Methodology for Measurement of Poverty in the country was constituted by the Planning Commission in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2012.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Expert Group under Dr. C. Rangarajan to review the methodology for measurement of poverty was constituted by the Planning Commission in 2012 (गरीबी मापने की पद्धति).

• The committee submitted its report in 2014.

• It was set up after criticism of the poverty estimates based on the Tendulkar Committee methodology.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Rangarajan Committee raised the poverty line to Rs. 32 per day in rural areas and Rs. 47 per day in urban areas.

• It estimated that about 29.5% of India's population was poor in 2011-12.

• Dr. C. Rangarajan is a noted economist and a former Governor of the RBI.

NOTE

• 2010 (Option 2): Not the year the Rangarajan Expert Group was constituted.

• 2008 (Option 3): Not correct; the Tendulkar Committee report came in 2009.

• 2006 (Option 4): Not the year of constitution of the Rangarajan poverty committee.

question: In which of the following years 'Sindh' was taken over by the East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1843.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sindh was annexed/taken over by the East India Company in 1843 (ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी).

• The annexation was carried out under Sir Charles Napier.

• After conquering Sindh, Napier is famously (though apocryphally) said to have sent the message 'Peccavi' (Latin for 'I have sinned' / 'I have Sindh').

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Governor-General at the time was Lord Ellenborough.

• The conquest of Sindh was a violation of earlier treaties with the Amirs (rulers) of Sindh.

• The annexation was strategically driven by fears of Russian and Afghan influence.

NOTE

• 1834 (Option 1): Not the year of the annexation of Sindh.

• 1856 (Option 3): The year Awadh (Oudh) was annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse-related policy of misgovernment.

• 1861 (Option 4): The year of the Indian Councils Act, 1861, not the annexation of Sindh.

question: In which year were regulations for underwriters issued by SEBI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1993.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SEBI (Underwriters) Regulations were issued in the year 1993 (अंडरराइटर्स के लिए विनियम).

• These regulations govern the registration and functioning of underwriters in the securities market.

• An underwriter agrees to buy the unsubscribed portion of a securities issue, guaranteeing capital to the issuer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) was established in 1988 and given statutory powers by the SEBI Act, 1992.

• SEBI is a regulatory body for the securities and capital markets in India.

• The headquarters of SEBI is in Mumbai.

NOTE

• 1991 (Option 1): The year of economic liberalisation (LPG reforms), not of the underwriter regulations.

• 1997 (Option 2): Not the year the SEBI Underwriters Regulations were issued.

• 1995 (Option 4): Not the correct year for these regulations.

question:
The Petroleum reserves of India are in which of the following region?
I. Sedimentary basins of Assam.
II. Off-shore region in the Arabian sea
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's petroleum reserves are found in both the sedimentary basins of Assam and the off-shore region in the Arabian Sea (पेट्रोलियम भंडार).

• Digboi (Assam) is where the first oil in India was discovered.

• Mumbai High (Bombay High) in the Arabian Sea is India's largest offshore oilfield.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Petroleum is a fossil fuel found in sedimentary rock formations.

• Other oil-producing regions in India include Gujarat (Ankleshwar) and the Krishna-Godavari basin.

• Petroleum products are refined into petrol, diesel, kerosene, LPG and other derivatives.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as offshore Arabian Sea reserves (Mumbai High) also exist.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as the sedimentary basins of Assam are also key petroleum reserves.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both regions do contain petroleum reserves.

question: The planning in the real sense began with _____ five year plan in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is second.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Planning in the real sense in India began with the Second Five Year Plan (दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना).

• The Second Plan (1956-1961) was based on the P. C. Mahalanobis model.

• It emphasised rapid industrialisation and the development of heavy and basic industries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

• The Second Plan led to the setting up of steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.

• Five Year Plans in India were formulated by the Planning Commission (established 1950), now replaced by NITI Aayog (2015).

NOTE

• fifth (Option 2): The Fifth Plan (1974-79) focused on 'Garibi Hatao' and removal of poverty and self-reliance.

• eighth (Option 3): The Eighth Plan (1992-97) focused on human resource development and followed the 1991 reforms.

• tenth (Option 4): The Tenth Plan (2002-07) aimed at doubling per capita income and reducing the poverty ratio.

question:
Which of the following was the focus of the Industrial Policy Statement, 1977?
I. Decentralisation of industries
II. Priority to small scale Industries
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Industrial Policy Statement, 1977 focused on both the decentralisation of industries and giving priority to small scale industries (औद्योगिक नीति वक्तव्य, 1977).

• It was introduced by the Janata Party government.

• It emphasised the development of small, tiny and cottage industries in rural and backward areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The policy introduced the concept of District Industries Centres (DICs).

• It aimed to reduce the concentration of economic power and generate employment in villages and small towns.

• The first Industrial Policy of independent India was the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since priority to small scale industries was also a key focus.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since decentralisation of industries was equally emphasised.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both were central features of the 1977 policy.

question:
Which of the following factor affect the distribution of population?
I. Topography
II. Climate
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both topography and climate are important factors affecting the distribution of population (जनसंख्या का वितरण).

• Plains and river valleys with gentle topography support dense populations, while rugged mountains are sparsely populated.

• A moderate/favourable climate attracts settlement, whereas extreme hot, cold or dry climates discourage it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Population distribution is influenced by physical factors (relief, climate, soil, water) and human factors (economy, social, political, culture).

• The Indo-Gangetic plains are among the most densely populated regions in India due to fertile soil and water.

• Density of population is the number of persons per unit area (persons per sq km).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since climate also affects population distribution.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since topography also affects population distribution.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both are recognised geographical factors.

question: Which of the following is NOT a push factor of migration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Better job opportunities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Better job opportunities is a pull factor, NOT a push factor of migration (प्रतिकर्ष कारक).

• Push factors are negative conditions at the origin that force people to leave (e.g., unemployment, poverty, disasters).

• Pull factors are positive conditions at the destination that attract people (e.g., jobs, better facilities, security).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Migration can be internal (within a country) or international (across countries).

• Push factors include natural calamities, war, unemployment and lack of amenities.

• Pull factors include better education, healthcare, higher wages and a better standard of living.

NOTE

• Unemployment (Option 1): A classic push factor that forces people to migrate away from the origin.

• Poor living conditions (Option 2): A push factor driving people to leave in search of a better life.

• Political turmoil (Option 3): A push factor, as instability and conflict compel people to migrate.

question: What becomes the major driving force in the movement of water in the xylem during the day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transpiration pull.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the day, transpiration pull becomes the major driving force in the movement of water in the xylem (वाष्पोत्सर्जन कर्षण).

• As water evaporates from the leaf surface (stomata) through transpiration, it creates a suction/tension that pulls water upward.

• This is explained by the Cohesion-Tension theory of water movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to the leaves; phloem transports food.

• Cohesion (water molecules sticking together) and adhesion (water sticking to xylem walls) aid the continuous water column.

• Transpiration also helps in cooling the plant and in the absorption/transport of minerals.

NOTE

• Root pressure (Option 2): A positive pressure important mainly at night when transpiration is low; it plays a minor role during the day.

• Active transport (Option 3): An energy-requiring process for ion/solute movement, not the main force for bulk water flow in xylem.

• Osmosis (Option 4): The movement of water across a semipermeable membrane; it helps water enter roots but is not the major driving force in the xylem during the day.

question: What is the primary function of the growth hormone in humans?
option_1: Controls metabolism of carbohydrates and fats
option_4: Regulates growth and development of the body
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regulates growth and development of the body.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary function of the growth hormone (GH / Somatotropin) is to regulate the growth and development of the body (वृद्धि हार्मोन).

• It is secreted by the anterior pituitary gland.

• It stimulates growth of bones, muscles and tissues.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Deficiency of GH in childhood causes dwarfism, while excess causes gigantism.

• Excess GH in adults leads to acromegaly (enlargement of hands, feet and facial bones).

• The pituitary gland is called the 'master gland' of the body.

NOTE

• Controls metabolism of carbohydrates and fats (Option 1): This is broadly associated with hormones like thyroxine and insulin/glucagon, not the primary role of growth hormone.

• Regulates blood sugar levels (Option 2): This is the primary function of insulin and glucagon from the pancreas.

• Maintains body temperature (Option 3): Body temperature regulation is controlled by the hypothalamus and thyroid hormone, not growth hormone.

question: During whose reign was the second Buddhist council was held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalashoka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Second Buddhist Council was held during the reign of Kalashoka (कालअशोक).

• It was held at Vaishali around 383 BCE, about a hundred years after the Buddha's death.

• It was presided over by Sabakami (Sabbakami).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Second Council led to the split of the Buddhist community into the Sthaviravadins and the Mahasanghikas.

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgriha under Ajatashatru, presided over by Mahakassapa.

• The Third Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka, and the Fourth in Kashmir under Kanishka.

NOTE

• Ajatashatru (Option 1): The Haryanka ruler during whose reign the First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgriha.

• Bimbisara (Option 2): The Haryanka king and contemporary of the Buddha, but no council was held in his reign.

• Mahapadma Nanda (Option 3... Option 4): The founder of the Nanda dynasty; no Buddhist council was held during his reign.
